items.prompt: Under what exact condition does a mutation fail with the board.version_conflict error?
items.answer: When an X-Board-Version header is sent and differs from the board's Version
distractors: Whenever two mutations hit the same board concurrently and race each other
When the request body's version field is older than the stored aggregate's
When the header is missing, since each mutation requires a version token
items.explanation: Omitting the header skips the check entirely. MutateAsync guards with `expectedVersion is not null && board.Version != expectedVersion.Value`, and ReadExpectedVersion returns null when the header is absent - the critique flags this opt-in design as risk 4.

items.prompt: A client calls move-column with position 999 on a board that has four columns. What happens?
items.answer: It lands at the end, with the position clamped and the columns reindexed
distractors: A 400 validation.non_negative error, because 999 is outside the column range
The column keeps position 999 and leaves a gap in the column ordering
A 409 conflict, since moving past the last slot implies a stale client
items.explanation: MoveColumn inserts at Math.Clamp(position, 0, _columns.Count) and then ReindexColumns rewrites every Position to its list index, a dense 0..n sequence - out-of-range input is normalized, not rejected.

items.prompt: The default 'Backlog' and 'Done' columns are created with cardLimit 0, while 'In progress' gets 4. What does a limit of 0 mean?
items.answer: Unlimited - the check throws only when CardLimit is positive and exceeded
distractors: The column is frozen and a 0-limit column rejects each AddCard with a conflict
The limit is unset, so it is inherited from the board's default of 10 cards
Zero is rejected at construction, so those columns always get a limit of 1
items.explanation: EnsureCardLimit's guard is `CardLimit > 0 && _cards.Count > CardLimit`, so 0 disables the check; a breach throws DomainException.Conflict with code column.card_limit.

items.prompt: MoveCard removes the card from its source column before adding it to the target, and the target's card-limit check can throw after the removal. Why is the stored board never left missing a card?
items.answer: UpdateAsync mutates a clone and stores it only on success, so a throw discards it
distractors: A compensating catch block re-inserts the card and rethrows the original error
The card-limit check runs before the removal, so the move cannot throw midway
The write lock rolls back the dictionary entry when the update delegate throws
items.explanation: The repository does `update(existing.Clone())` and assigns `_boards[boardId]` only after update returns; a thrown invariant propagates before the assignment, abandoning the half-mutated copy and leaving the last consistent clone in place.

items.prompt: DELETE /api/boards/{id}/cards/{id} routes to ArchiveCardAsync. What does 'archiving' actually do to the card?
items.answer: It removes the card from its column and discards it - an irreversible delete
distractors: It moves the card to a hidden Archive column and keeps it there for restores
It flags the card IsArchived, so that list responses can filter it out later
It serializes the card to disk before removal, so it can be restored later
items.explanation: Nothing stores archived cards. Board.ArchiveCard is RemoveCard + Touch; the Card instance is simply discarded. The name promises more than the implementation delivers - a good review catch.

items.prompt: A create-card request carries an assigneeId that is a valid GUID but belongs to nobody on the board. What comes back?
items.answer: A 400 member.not_found problem, as assignees have to be members
distractors: A 404, since the referenced member resource does not exist anywhere
A 201 - assignees are free-form GUIDs, and membership goes unchecked
A 409 conflict flagging a stale member list held by the client
items.explanation: EnsureAssigneeExists scans _members and throws DomainException.BadRequest("member.not_found", "Assignee is not a member of this board.") when no id matches; null assignees are allowed.

items.prompt: How does a DomainException thrown deep in the aggregate reach the HTTP client?
items.answer: Middleware catches it and writes problem+json with its status, code and traceId
distractors: Each endpoint wraps its service call in try/catch and maps codes to Results
ASP.NET's developer exception page serializes it as HTML in each environment
The service layer converts it into a Result<T> that the endpoints match on
items.explanation: ExceptionHandlingMiddleware has catch arms for DomainException (its own StatusCode), BadHttpRequestException (400) and everything else (500, detail hidden outside Development); WriteProblemAsync writes application/problem+json and adds the code and traceId to ProblemDetails.Extensions.

items.prompt: A mutation arrives with the header 'X-Board-Version: abc'. What is the outcome?
items.answer: 400 board.version_invalid, since int.TryParse fails on it
distractors: The header is ignored as if absent, and the mutation proceeds
409 board.version_conflict, since 'abc' differs from the version
500 server.unhandled, since int.Parse throws a FormatException
items.explanation: ReadExpectedVersion distinguishes absent (null, check skipped) from present-but-unparsable, which throws DomainException.BadRequest("board.version_invalid", ...) via int.TryParse.

items.prompt: Why can code that fetched a Board via GetAsync freely call mutators on it without corrupting the stored state?
items.answer: The repository hands out a deep Clone, so callers hold a detached copy
distractors: Board instances are immutable records, so mutators return new objects
GetAsync takes the write lock, so the caller has exclusive access to it
It is not safe - mutating a fetched board quietly mutates the shared store
items.explanation: Stored boards never escape: GetAsync returns `stored.Clone()` (and UpdateAsync both mutates a clone and stores a clone). Board.Clone deep-copies columns and cards, giving clone-in/clone-out isolation.

items.prompt: What must a caller prove before PATCHing a card on someone's board in this codebase?
items.answer: Nothing, as endpoints skip identity checks and members are display data
distractors: Board membership, enforced by the EnsureAssigneeExists guard on all writes
A valid session cookie and CSRF token from the client app's login flow
Possession of the board's version token, acting as a capability secret
items.explanation: The guide's auth-boundary section: no RequireAuthorization, no [Authorize], no identity checks; members live in seed storage as display data, not security principals. The assignee guard validates data, not callers.

items.front: NetTrello's Guard.Required does more than validate. What exactly does the stored value look like?
items.back: The value is trimmed first; whitespace-only input throws validation.required, over-length trimmed input throws validation.max_length, and the TRIMMED string is what the domain keeps - normalization and validation in one step.

items.front: A board fresh out of POST /api/boards already reports Version 5. Walk through why.
items.back: The constructor starts Version at 1, then CreateBoardAsync adds the four default columns (Backlog, In progress, Review, Done) and every AddColumn calls Touch, which increments Version - 1 + 4 bumps = 5.

items.front: The critique ranks 'optional version header' as risk 4. What is the failure mode and the recommended fix?
items.back: Because ReadExpectedVersion returns null when X-Board-Version is absent, any client can bypass optimistic-concurrency conflict checks and overwrite newer state; the recommendation is to require the header on all mutations.
